which Dell says gives developers the ability to dedicate the machine to an external hypervisor-based virtual machine without slowing the machine's host applications. We of course did not test that feature.
Dell's Dynamically Adjustable Backlight control boosts brightness slightly by employing sensors to gauge ambient lighting conditions. The result is an “adaptive tone according to the surrounding brightness.” Upon unpacking, we discovered the brightness set to a comfortable midpoint suitable for indoor tasks.
The Dell XPS 13 Developer Edition has some unfinished aspects. It's important to note it's been available, as a pilot project, for a while now, and as a result doesn't include such niceties as Bluetooth, a docking-compatible port, or an HDMI port. We'd preferred to see the 2.0 USB ports rather than the 1.1 ones. The display is good, but it could have been enhanced with a full 1920 x 1080 resolution.
Neither does an "easy" mechanism exist for a practice that has become commonplace. Feedback from customers has driven the "telemedicine" movement, enabling doctors to diagnose patients through computer screens and typing online. The same goes for the “telecommuting” movement that's evolved. To that end, we'd likely need an extra USB mouse and/or keyboard.
Surprisingly, even though Ubuntu's Control Center misses some features present in other systems, the support for hardware in Linux is continuously improving. Among the primary hardware items we tested, only one didn't function correctly: WiFi. We ran the system diagnostic tool, which confirmed that the wired connection was operational and that the wireless adaptor had been identified. It simply couldn't connect at all. We were able to connect wirelessly to the Wi-Fi router by walking into the room, but we received no signal when attempting to access the XPS 13 Developer Edition wirelessly. The testing video, shown below, captures that moment, while it is also featured in the product photo gallery at the top of this page.
Better yet, it was really easy to send the BIOS, WiFi, and the other boot-related numbers out to Dell and let it debug the system
